citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the SVD-entropy, Petrosian, Renyi and Tsallis cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::dispersionEntropy(c=6, dimension=3, delay=1): standardize (sample sd) -> normal CDF (NCDF) -> c amplitude classes -> length-m dispersion patterns -> DispEn = normalized Shannon entropy of the pattern distribution / ln(c^m); reverse=TRUE gives RDEn. The reference re-computes DispEn and RDEn with NeuroKit2 entropy_dispersion across (c,dimension,delay) settings, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the SVD-entropy, Petrosian, Renyi and Tsallis cases). Dispersion entropy (Rostaghi & Azami 2016) is a symbolic-dynamics complexity measure with a mechanism distinct from the amplitude-histogram entropies (Renyi/Tsallis, which bin amplitudes) and from ordinal permutation entropy (which uses rank order): it maps the signal to c amplitude classes through the normal CDF (outlier-robust), forms length-m embedding vectors (dispersion patterns), and takes the Shannon entropy of the pattern distribution normalized by ln(c^m). dispersionEntropy is a NEW op. It reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_dispersion BIT-FOR-BIT for both DispEn (max |diff| 0) and the reverse dispersion entropy RDEn (max |diff| ~7e-18) across (c,dimension,delay) settings. On real eyes-closed POz EEG the signal realizes only 108 of the 216 (=c^m) possible dispersion patterns -- structured, not pattern-saturating. HONEST: the NCDF classes are near-equiprobable by construction (1/c target); the complexity lives in the pattern (embedding) distribution, not the marginal. The normalization follows NeuroKit2 exactly (base-2 Shannon term / natural-log ln(c^m)), so DispEn ranges in [0, 1/ln2 = 1.443]; this convention is reproduced, not corrected.
